title: Add transform rule registry and coverage gates
description:
Introduce deterministic transform rule metadata and pre-emit coverage checks before building substantial C# emission.

Scope:
- Define transform rule metadata for source language, input node kind or feature kind, output feature where relevant, status, and version.
- Store or expose rule definitions in a queryable form compatible with Datomic facts.
- Implement coverage checks that verify each reachable source construct has exactly one applicable implemented rule or an explicit unsupported/stubbed status.
- Produce actionable coverage failures with source file, source span, node/feature kind, and missing/ambiguous rule information.
- Support an explicit stub/unsupported mode boundary without silently emitting nonsense.

Out of scope:
- Full C# emitter implementation.
- Compiler diagnostic ingestion.
- Advanced transform behavior beyond metadata and coverage gating.

Acceptance criteria:
- Rule metadata can be registered and queried by source language and node/feature kind.
- Coverage gates fail clearly for missing or ambiguous rules.
- Coverage gates pass when representative source facts are fully covered or explicitly stubbed.
- Tests cover implemented, unsupported, missing, and ambiguous rule cases.
- clojure -T:build test passes.
- br sync --flush-only is run before committing.

title: Set up Vibeformer project dependencies and usage smoke tests
description:
Set up Vibeformer's first external project dependencies and focused usage tests, limited to dependency wiring and proof-of-use.

Scope:
- Add the initial dependencies needed for Java analysis via Spoon, Kotlin parsing/analysis research, and local Datomic.
- Add small usage tests that prove each dependency can be loaded and exercised from the Clojure project.
- Keep this to project setup; do not implement the normalized fact schema, full extractors, transform rules, or C# emission yet.

Done when:
- The Spoon, Kotlin parsing libs, and local Datomic subtasks are complete.
- The project test command passes with the new dependency smoke tests.
- Any important dependency/version constraints are documented in code comments, test names, or README notes where appropriate.

title: Add Spoon dependency and Java parser smoke tests
description:
Add Spoon as the initial Java frontend dependency for Vibeformer and prove it can parse Java source in the direction this project needs.

Scope:
- Add the Spoon dependency/version to the Clojure project.
- Add a focused usage test that parses a small Java sample containing project-relevant constructs such as package, class, field, method, modifiers, type references, method calls, and source positions.
- Assert enough of the Spoon model to make the example useful for later normalized fact extraction.
- Keep the test as an example for the Kotlin parsing setup to learn from.

Out of scope:
- Full Java extractor implementation.
- Datomic fact schema or persistence.
- C# transform/emission logic.

title: Add Kotlin parsing dependencies and smoke tests
description:
Add the initial Kotlin parsing/analysis dependencies and prove they can parse or analyze Kotlin source from the Clojure project.

Scope:
- Research and choose starting dependency coordinates for Kotlin parsing, using Kotlin PSI and Kotlin Analysis API as the leading candidates.
- Let the Spoon smoke test guide the shape of this test: parse a small Kotlin sample and assert project-relevant constructs such as package, class/object/function/property, type references, nullability where available, calls, and source positions.
- Document which Kotlin APIs are being exercised and any classpath or environment caveats.

Out of scope:
- Full Kotlin extractor implementation.
- Complete semantic resolution for all Kotlin constructs.
- Datomic fact schema or persistence.
- C# transform/emission logic.

title: Add local Datomic dependency and embedded database smoke tests
description:
Add Datomic Local for Vibeformer analysis/control-plane storage and prove a local embedded database can be used from tests.

Dependency target:
- com.datomic/local {:mvn/version "1.0.291"}

Scope:
- Add the Datomic Local dependency to the Clojure project.
- Add a focused usage test that creates/connects to a local test database, transacts a tiny Vibeformer-shaped fact such as a file/source-node/declaration placeholder, and queries it back.
- Keep test data disposable and isolated so it can run repeatedly in local development/CI.
- Document any required local storage, cleanup, or licensing/authentication caveats discovered during setup.

Out of scope:
- Full Datomic schema design.
- Full source fact ingestion.
- Transform rule storage or compiler diagnostic ingestion.

title: Extract normalized Java facts with Spoon
description:
Use Spoon to extract normalized Java facts from ingested Java file records and transact them into Datomic.

Scope:
- Read Java file facts produced by pkl-onf.
- Parse Java files with Spoon without modifying ../research/pkl.
- Populate source nodes, declarations, source-language types, symbol/type refs where available, and Java feature facts using the schema from pkl-q1v.
- Preserve stable identities so reruns update existing logical facts instead of creating duplicates.
- Capture source spans and source hashes for extracted nodes.
- Record unresolved references explicitly with reasons when classpath or model data is missing.

Out of scope:
- Kotlin extraction.
- C# emission, transform rules, type mapping to C#, or diagnostics ingestion.
- Complete Java language coverage beyond the constructs needed for the first research/pkl inventory pass.

Acceptance criteria:
- Java classes, interfaces, enums, fields, constructors, methods, modifiers, packages, inheritance/interface implementation, method calls, type refs, and basic feature facts are queryable in Datomic.
- Re-running extraction is idempotent for unchanged files.
- Tests cover representative Java fixtures and Datomic queries over nodes, declarations, types, refs, and features.
- clojure -T:build test passes.
- br sync --flush-only is run before committing.

title: Run dotnet build and capture sample diagnostics
description:
Parent: pkl-nb1.

Wire the sample harness to run dotnet build once target/csharp contains a generated project, following implementation-plan steps 11 and 12. Build failures should become structured diagnostics that guide transformer work.

Scope:
- Invoke dotnet build from the sample runner when a .csproj exists.
- Capture stdout, stderr, exit code, and compiler diagnostics under target/diagnostics.
- Parse useful diagnostic fields where practical: code, severity, message, file, line, and column.
- Include sample name, source root, target project path, stage, and command context in failures.
- Keep build failure as a sample-run result with actionable diagnostics.

Acceptance criteria:
- clojure -T:build sample runs dotnet build for java-word-count once project generation exists.
- target/diagnostics contains raw build logs and structured EDN diagnostics.
- A failing compile reports enough context to identify the transform gap.
- clojure -T:build test passes, with tests isolated from machines without dotnet where needed.
- br sync --flush-only is run before finishing.

title: Implement initial source-to-C# type mapping
description:
Implement the first explicit, queryable mapping layer from Java/Kotlin source types to C# type names/usings/helpers.

Scope:
- Map Java primitives, boxed primitives, String, BigDecimal, BigInteger, arrays, common collections, Optional, exceptions, and project-local types.
- Map Kotlin nullable types, Kotlin primitives/strings, collections, function type syntax where feasible, and project-local types.
- Represent required usings and helper requirements alongside mapped C# type strings.
- Keep mappings deterministic and testable against source type facts from Datomic.
- Leave room for later project/framework-specific mappings discovered from research/pkl.

Out of scope:
- Statement/expression emission.
- Project generation.
- Full Kotlin semantic resolution beyond what existing type facts provide.
- Runtime compatibility helper implementation except for naming required helpers.

Acceptance criteria:
- Type mapping functions/facts are queryable and deterministic.
- Tests cover primitive, boxed, string, collection, nullable, array, exception, optional, and project-local cases.
- Missing mappings fail clearly with enough source type context to drive future work.
- clojure -T:build test passes.
- br sync --flush-only is run before committing.

title: Emit basic Java declarations as C# skeletons
description:
Parent: pkl-nb1.

Implement the first deterministic C# emission pass for Java declaration facts. This follows implementation-plan step 6 and should produce disposable C# under sample-projects/<name>/target/csharp.

Scope:
- Emit namespace and type declarations for Java classes.
- Emit field declarations for simple static/final fields where enough type facts exist.
- Emit constructor and method signatures, including static main and package-private methods.
- Preserve generated folder structure by source package/namespace.
- Keep method bodies stubbed where statement emission is not implemented yet.

Acceptance criteria:
- clojure -T:build sample creates at least one .cs file for java-word-count under target/csharp.
- Generated C# is regenerated from facts and remains disposable.
- Tests cover declaration emission from a small Java fixture.
- clojure -T:build test passes.
- br sync --flush-only is run before finishing.

title: Generate disposable C# project files for sample runs
description:
Parent: pkl-nb1.

Add project generation for sample target/csharp output, following implementation-plan step 10. This should make emitted C# buildable as a normal disposable .NET project once emission is complete enough.

Scope:
- Generate a .csproj under sample-projects/<name>/target/csharp.
- Choose a deterministic target framework and nullable/implicit using settings for early validation.
- Generate source file paths from source packages/namespaces without changing committed sample source.
- Make project generation part of clojure -T:build sample.
- Keep target/csharp scratch output ignored by git.

Acceptance criteria:
- clojure -T:build sample creates a .csproj for java-word-count under target/csharp.
- The project includes generated .cs files from the sample emitter.
- Tests verify deterministic project generation for a fixture sample.
- clojure -T:build test passes.
- br sync --flush-only is run before finishing.

title: Build feature inventory queries and reports
description:
Implement reusable feature inventory queries and reports over the normalized Datomic facts.

Scope:
- Turn the documented Datomic inventory queries into tested Clojure functions.
- Count features by kind/status/language and rank unsupported features by occurrence and affected file count.
- Report unsupported features by source file.
- Report files with no unsupported features.
- Provide a small API or task-friendly function for summarizing the current research/pkl inventory.
- Keep queries stable enough to guide implementation ordering for transform work.

Out of scope:
- Extracting new facts from source files.
- Defining transform rules or emitting C#.
- Compiler diagnostic ingestion.

Acceptance criteria:
- Feature inventory functions run against Datomic Local test data and return deterministic, useful summaries.
- Queries can rank unsupported Java/Kotlin features by count and file spread.
- Tests cover mixed supported/unsupported features, multiple files, and files with no unsupported features.
- clojure -T:build test passes.
- br sync --flush-only is run before committing.

title: Register initial Java transform coverage rules for java-word-count
description:
Parent: pkl-nb1.

Based on clojure -T:build sample, java-word-count currently reaches analysis but coverage/check reports 18 missing-rule failures. Add the first transform rule catalog entries needed by this sample so coverage failures move from missing-rule to deliberate implemented, stubbed, or unsupported statuses.

Scope:
- Register rules for Java class, constructor, field, method, and method-call node kinds observed in WordCounter.java.
- Register feature rules for java.feature/class, java.feature/field, java.feature/package-private-member, and java.feature/checked-exception.
- Make rule registration part of the sample pipeline before coverage/check.
- Keep unsupported or not-yet-emitted behavior explicit with stubbed or unsupported rule status rather than absent rules.

Acceptance criteria:
- clojure -T:build sample no longer reports missing-rule failures for java-word-count constructs.
- coverage.edn names the rule that covers or rejects each remaining construct.
- clojure -T:build test passes.
- br sync --flush-only is run before finishing.

title: Add Kotlin semantic resolution with Analysis API
description:
Add Kotlin Analysis API support to enrich Kotlin PSI facts with semantic type and symbol resolution.

Scope:
- Build the minimal module/session/classpath setup needed for Kotlin Analysis API over the ingested research/pkl Kotlin sources.
- Resolve declarations, call targets, property/function symbols, receiver/owner types, and expression/type references where the API and classpath permit.
- Update existing Kotlin facts idempotently with resolved target/type links.
- Store unresolved refs with explicit reasons such as missing classpath, unsupported construct, or analysis API limitation.
- Document classpath/session constraints discovered during implementation.

Out of scope:
- Initial Kotlin PSI syntax extraction.
- Java extraction.
- C# emission, transform rules, or diagnostics ingestion.

Acceptance criteria:
- Kotlin refs and type facts are semantically resolved for representative fixtures where dependencies are available.
- Unresolved Kotlin refs are stored deliberately with reasons instead of being dropped.
- Re-running semantic enrichment is idempotent.
- Tests cover resolved and unresolved cases.
- clojure -T:build test passes.
- br sync --flush-only is run before committing.

title: Record source-to-C# provenance for generated sample output
description:
Parent: pkl-nb1.

Replace the current skipped provenance placeholder with source-to-destination provenance for emitted files and rules, following implementation-plan step 13.

Scope:
- Record which source file, node, declaration, feature, and transform rule produced each generated C# file or span where available.
- Write target/provenance.edn for sample runs.
- Include rule id/version and enough target path information to relate compiler diagnostics back to source facts.
- Keep provenance deterministic and regenerated with target output.

Acceptance criteria:
- clojure -T:build sample writes provenance.edn with real mappings instead of pipeline.stage/not-implemented.
- Provenance can connect generated WordCounter.cs entries back to WordCounter.java source ids.
- Tests cover deterministic provenance output for a fixture emission.
- clojure -T:build test passes.
- br sync --flush-only is run before finishing.

title: End-to-end sample project run harness
description:
Create a Vibeformer integration-run path for committed sample Java/Kotlin projects under vibeformer/sample-projects. The durable input is each sample's source/ tree; all emitted C# and run artifacts go under the sample's gitignored target/ tree.

Scope:
- Discover sample projects and their source roots.
- Run analysis against a selected sample project.
- Emit generated C# into sample-projects/<name>/target/csharp.
- Add a compile step using dotnet build once project generation exists.
- Capture diagnostics under target/diagnostics.
- Capture optional exported facts and provenance under target/facts and target/provenance.edn.
- Make the java-word-count sample the first smoke target.

Acceptance criteria:
- A developer can invoke one command from vibeformer to run the java-word-count sample end to end through the supported pipeline stages.
- Generated C# and run artifacts are disposable and remain ignored by git.
- Failures report enough sample name, source path, stage, and diagnostic context to guide transformer work.
- The harness can add more sample projects without changing core test code.

Implementation-plan links:
- Supports whole-project compile tests.
- Prepares project generation, dotnet build validation, diagnostic ingestion, and source-to-destination provenance work.
- Keeps generated C# as scratch output rather than durable state.

title: Ingest Java/Kotlin source files from research/pkl into Datomic
description:
Build the source ingestion pass that discovers Java and Kotlin files under ../research/pkl and stores file-level facts in Datomic idempotently and efficiently. This epic stops at project/file metadata; parser-derived source nodes, declarations, refs, types, and features belong to later extractor epics.

Scope:
- Discover .java and .kt files under ../research/pkl without modifying that tree.
- Compute stable project/file identities compatible with the canonical Datomic schema.
- Capture file path, language, content hash, project association, and package only via a lightweight text scan when practical.
- Make ingestion idempotent: repeated runs update changed file facts and do not create duplicate logical file records.
- Make ingestion efficient enough for repeated development runs: avoid retransacting unchanged files when the stored hash matches.
- Provide a small API/entrypoint that can run against Datomic Local in tests.
- Add tests using temporary fixture trees plus, if practical, a guarded smoke path for ../research/pkl discovery.

Out of scope:
- Spoon model extraction, Kotlin PSI extraction, Kotlin Analysis API use, or any parser-backed AST walk.
- Source nodes, declarations, semantic types, symbol refs, feature facts, transform rules, or C# emission.
- Modifying ../research/pkl.

Acceptance criteria:
- The ingestion pass can discover Java and Kotlin source files from a configured source root.
- File facts transact into Datomic using the schema from pkl-q1v.
- Re-running ingestion against unchanged files performs no duplicate logical inserts and can skip unchanged content.
- Changed files update hash/package metadata deterministically.
- Tests cover Java files, Kotlin files, non-source-file filtering, idempotent reruns, and changed-file updates.
- clojure -T:build test passes.
- br sync --flush-only is run before committing.

title: Emit java-word-count statement and expression subset
description:
Parent: pkl-nb1.

Implement the basic Java statement and expression emission needed for WordCounter.java, following implementation-plan step 9. The goal is deterministic C# body output for the sample, not a broad Java emitter.

Scope:
- Extract or model any missing statement/expression facts needed for return, if, local variable declarations, simple method calls, static member access, field access, array length, and member access chains.
- Emit C# for WordCounter.countWords and WordCounter.main bodies where supported.
- Map string trim/isEmpty, Regex split length, console output/error, Environment.Exit, Path/File read, and internal static method calls as explicit transform cases or helper requirements.
- Leave unsupported constructs as clear diagnostics, not silent omissions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Generated WordCounter.cs contains non-stub bodies for countWords and main where facts support them.
- Remaining unsupported expressions are reported with source path, span, and rule context.
- Unit or golden tests cover the emitted statement/expression subset.
- clojure -T:build test passes.
- br sync --flush-only is run before finishing.

title: Datomic schema for files, nodes, declarations, types, refs, features
description:
**Implementation Plan**

Build this as a small schema foundation, not as extractor work yet.

1. Add a schema namespace:
   - Create `src/vibeformer/datomic/schema.clj`.
   - Expose `schema` or `all` as pure Datomic tx-data.
   - Optional helper: `install! [conn]` wrapping `(d/transact conn {:tx-data all})`.
   - Keep no new dependencies.

2. Define stable identity conventions:
   - Add minimal `:project/id` because `:file/project` already appears in the model docs.
   - Use `:file/id` as the file identity, not only `:file/path`, so multiple projects can contain the same relative path.
   - Keep `:file/path` indexed/queryable.
   - Use unique identity attrs for `:node/id`, `:decl/id`, `:type/id`, `:ref/id`, and `:feature/id`.

3. Implement schema groups:
   - Project/file attrs: project id/name/root, file id/path/lang/hash/project/package.
   - Node attrs: id/lang/kind/name/file/parent/ordinal/source span/source hash.
   - Declaration attrs: id/lang/kind/name/qualified-name/source-node/return-type/type/modifiers.
   - Type attrs: id/lang/name/nullable flag, plus ordered type-argument support via small arg entities if needed.
   - Reference attrs: id/kind/from-node/to-decl/to-type/name/owner-type/resolved flag/reason.
   - Feature attrs: id/lang/kind/node/status/severity.

4. Refactor the existing Datomic smoke test:
   - Remove the inline `datomic-smoke-schema` from `test/vibeformer/vibeformer_test.clj`.
   - Use the new schema namespace in the existing Datomic Local test.
   - Transact a richer fixture covering file, node, declaration, type, resolved ref, unresolved ref, and feature.
   - Assert the key joins needed by the next steps:
     - file -> node -> declaration
     - declaration -> return/type
     - ref -> source node -> optional target declaration/type
     - feature inventory counts by kind/status
     - unsupported features by file

5. Add focused schema tests:
   - New test namespace is probably cleaner: `test/vibeformer/datomic/schema_test.clj`.
   - Verify the schema transacts into a fresh Datomic Local in-memory DB.
   - Verify lookup refs work for every unique identity attr.
   - Verify re-transacting an entity by identity updates facts rather than duplicating logical records.
   - Verify ordered fields that matter, especially node ordinal and any type-arg ordinal approach.

6. Update docs:
   - Update `doc/datomic-model.md` to reflect any concrete schema decisions, especially `:file/id` and ordered type argument representation if used.
   - Keep README unchanged unless a new quick-start command is added, which is unlikely.

7. Validation:
   - Run `clojure -T:build test`.
   - Run `git diff --check`.
   - Run `br sync --flush-only` before committing, per repo workflow.

**Out Of Scope**

No extractor changes, no Spoon/Kotlin fact emission, no feature inventory CLI, no transform/emitter work, and no durable Datomic storage setup. This step only creates the canonical schema and proves it supports the fact graph shape the next implementation steps will need.

**Epic Acceptance Criteria**

The epic is done when Vibeformer has a reusable Datomic schema namespace, tests transact and query a representative file/node/decl/type/ref/feature graph in Datomic Local, the old inline smoke schema is gone, docs match the implemented schema, and `clojure -T:build test` passes.

title: Extract normalized Kotlin syntax facts with Kotlin PSI
description:
Use Kotlin PSI to extract syntax-level Kotlin facts from ingested Kotlin file records and transact them into Datomic.

Scope:
- Read Kotlin file facts produced by pkl-onf.
- Parse Kotlin files with Kotlin PSI without modifying ../research/pkl.
- Populate source nodes, syntax declarations, source-language type syntax, syntactic refs where available, and Kotlin feature facts using the schema from pkl-q1v.
- Model Kotlin-specific syntax explicitly, including nullability, safe calls, Elvis expressions, object declarations, companion objects, top-level declarations, properties, and functions.
- Preserve stable identities so reruns update existing logical facts instead of creating duplicates.
- Capture text-offset-derived source spans and source hashes for extracted nodes.

Out of scope:
- Kotlin Analysis API semantic resolution.
- Java extraction.
- C# emission, transform rules, type mapping to C#, or diagnostics ingestion.

Acceptance criteria:
- Kotlin files, packages, classes, objects, top-level functions, properties, nullable type syntax, call expressions, safe calls, Elvis expressions, companion/object declarations, and source spans are queryable in Datomic.
- Re-running extraction is idempotent for unchanged files.
- Tests cover representative Kotlin fixtures and Datomic queries over nodes, declarations, type syntax, refs/features, and source spans.
- clojure -T:build test passes.
- br sync --flush-only is run before committing.
